response.summary: The endpoint works but puts data access, provider HTTP calls and business rules in the controller, bypassing the existing Application/Infrastructure layers.

findings.title: Controller does data access and payment orchestration
findings.detail: PaymentsController opens a SqlConnection, reads and updates Orders and calls providers directly. OrderService.MarkPaidAsync and IPaymentGateway already exist for this, so the change duplicates logic in the wrong layer (guideline: Controllers stay thin).
findings.recommendation: Inject OrderService and a keyed IPaymentGateway; keep the controller to request mapping and status codes.

findings.title: New HttpClient created per request
findings.detail: `var http = new HttpClient();` inside the action causes socket exhaustion under load and ignores DNS changes (guideline: HTTP clients).
findings.recommendation: Use a typed client from IHttpClientFactory (StripeGateway already does).

findings.title: No test seam for payment flow
findings.detail: All logic is in one action with concrete SqlConnection/HttpClient, so the paid/failed paths cannot be unit tested.
findings.recommendation: Resolves itself once the logic moves behind OrderService and IPaymentGateway.
